pr_body:
Added more tests to SQLColAttribute as well as a framework that allows different types to test each field.

Also made the code more concise in the SQLColAttribute function and altered the way the DescRecord gets set so that each function related to it will return the same information instead of calculating it separately. 

Potentially solves #6321
pr_comments: I just added support for `SQL_C_SHORT` and `SQL_C_TINYINT` in the fetching.

issue_context.title: ODBC issue with System.Data.Odbc GetSchema()
issue_context.body:
### What happens?

Calling .Net 4.8 System.Data.Odbc GetSchema() on a DuckDB ODBC connection fails. When running my C# program in the debugger an exception occurs. Debugger and call stack are not much help given I'm using ODBC and Microsoft doesn't let you step into .Net code (at least not System.Data.Odbc). 

I also have a VBScript program that uses ADO. I made a small program that uses ADO OpenSchema and that works just fine. Under the hood it calls a query to get schema table info that is very similar to DuckDB, but not exactly the same (more on that below). So it would seem this problem may be isolated to System.Data.ODBC.

```
        dim adSchemaTables: adSchemaTables = 20
        dim rsTables: Set rsTables = objConn.OpenSchema(adSchemaTables) 
        While Not rsTables.EOF
            dim ff: for each ff in rsTables.Fields
                log ff.name & " " & ff.type & " " & ff.value
            next
            rsTables.MoveNext
        Wend
```


### To Reproduce

DuckDB built using Visual Studio 2019 from Github source "switched" to Branch_V0.7.0. I use a batch file that follows the process of the make file. Here is the relevant cmake from that

```
    cmake -S ..\.. -B . -GNinja ^
        -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release  ^
        -DBUILD_ICU_EXTENSION=1  ^
        -DBUILD_PARQUET_EXTENSION=1  ^
        -DBUILD_TPCH_EXTENSION=1  ^
        -DBUILD_TPCDS_EXTENSION=1  ^
        -DBUILD_FTS_EXTENSION=1  ^
        -DBUILD_JSON_EXTENSION=1  ^
        -DBUILD_EXCEL_EXTENSION=1  ^
        -DBUILD_ODBC_DRIVER=1  ^
        -DDISABLE_UNITY=0 ^
        -DBUILD_PYTHON=0
    cmake --build . --config Release
```
I used the Windows ODBC Data Source Admin tools to run traces, and I added some cout log messages to the DuckDB ODBC driver to try to see what was going on. It turns out that System.Data.ODBC was passing a list of tables that it wanted DuckDB to use to query the schema. Specifically `TABLE,SYSTEM TABLE`  as shown in the ODBC trace below:

```
DemoDbViewer.ex 16b8-2114	ENTER SQLTablesW 
		HSTMT               0x0000019A2550E870
		WCHAR *             0x0000000000000000 <null pointer>
		SWORD                        0 
		WCHAR *             0x0000000000000000 <null pointer>
		SWORD                        0 
		WCHAR *             0x0000000000000000 <null pointer>
		SWORD                        0 
		WCHAR *             0x0000019A0CE4E584 [      18] "TABLE,SYSTEM TABLE"
		SWORD                       18 

DemoDbViewer.ex 16b8-2114	EXIT  SQLTablesW  with return code 0 (SQL_SUCCESS)
		HSTMT               0x0000019A2550E870
		WCHAR *             0x0000000000000000 <null pointer>
		SWORD                        0 
		WCHAR *             0x0000000000000000 <null pointer>
		SWORD                        0 
		WCHAR *             0x0000000000000000 <null pointer>
		SWORD                        0 
		WCHAR *             0x0000019A0CE4E584 [      18] "TABLE,SYSTEM TABLE"
		SWORD                       18 
```
The code to handle that is `M:\github\duckdb-v0.7.0\tools\odbc\statement.cpp` around line 320 where it uses regex to do some substitutions as part of building up the schema query. The resulting query is

```
SELECT
         table_catalog::VARCHAR "TABLE_CAT"
       , table_schema "TABLE_SCHEM"
       , table_name "TABLE_NAME"
       , CASE WHEN table_type='BASE TABLE' THEN 'TABLE' ELSE table_type
         END "TABLE_TYPE"
       , '' "REMARKS"
FROM
         information_schema.tables
WHERE
         COALESCE("TABLE_SCHEM",'main') LIKE 'main'
         AND COALESCE("TABLE_NAME",'')  LIKE '%'
         AND table_type IN ('BASE TABLE'
                          , SYSTEM 'BASE TABLE')               <----------------<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<
ORDER BY
         TABLE_TYPE
       , TABLE_CATALOG
       , TABLE_SCHEMA
       , TABLE_NAME"
```
The issue is there is no table `SYSTEM TABLE` and the regex kind of botches things up resulting in an invalid query. This can be fixed by removing ` , SYSTEM 'BASE TABLE')`. The result should run in the command line client. 

My quick and dirty fix was to add the following in front of the other regex_replace() calls which just gets rid of the `SYSTEM TABLE`. Not a production solution but good enough to move past this particular issue.

> 		table_tp = std::regex_replace(table_tp, std::regex("('SYSTEM TABLE'|SYSTEM TABLE)"), "");

Turns out that was not the only issue, however. The exception then changed to an overflow. Using the ODBC trace log I was able to track where the issue was happening. It was right after this
```
DemoDbViewer.ex 16b8-2114	ENTER SQLColAttributeW 
		SQLHSTMT            0x0000019A2550E870
		SQLSMALLINT                  1 
		SQLSMALLINT                  4 <unknown>
		SQLPOINTER         0x0000019A0C98DEE0
		SQLSMALLINT               4096 
		SQLSMALLINT *       0x000000989EDFDFB8
		SQLPOINTER          0x000000989EDFDF58

DemoDbViewer.ex 16b8-2114	EXIT  SQLColAttributeW  with return code 0 (SQL_SUCCESS)
		SQLHSTMT            0x0000019A2550E870
		SQLSMALLINT                  1 
		SQLSMALLINT                  4 <unknown>
		SQLPOINTER         0x0000019A0C98DEE0
		SQLSMALLINT               4096 
		SQLSMALLINT *       0x000000989EDFDFB8 (0)
		SQLPOINTER          0x000000989EDFDF58 (-1)
```
Here the 4 <unknown> is `SQL_COLUMN_PRECISION`. The code to handle this is in the same file as previous issue, on or around line 564 (search for `case SQL_COLUMN_PRECISION:`). As coded, it returns a value of -1 which is the value that was in `desc_record->sql_desc_precision` for this particular column. After a bunch of digging on the internet, I found a reference that says for CHAR and related (in this case VARCHAR) it should return the size of the string buffer. So I hard coded a value of 4096. This is another obviously non-production fix, but I was able to get away with it as the Schema table was all VARCHARs, and it allowed me to move on.

The ODBC trace now indicated an issue with `SQL_COLUMN_SCALE` which is `5`:
```
DemoDbViewer.ex 16b8-2114	ENTER SQLColAttributeW 
		SQLHSTMT            0x0000019A2550E870
		SQLSMALLINT                  1 
		SQLSMALLINT                  5 <unknown>
		SQLPOINTER         0x0000019A0C98DEE0
		SQLSMALLINT               4096 
		SQLSMALLINT *       0x000000989EDFDFB8
		SQLPOINTER          0x000000989EDFDF58

DemoDbViewer.ex 16b8-2114	EXIT  SQLColAttributeW  with return code 0 (SQL_SUCCESS)
		SQLHSTMT            0x0000019A2550E870
		SQLSMALLINT                  1 
		SQLSMALLINT                  5 <unknown>
		SQLPOINTER         0x0000019A0C98DEE0
		SQLSMALLINT               4096 
		SQLSMALLINT *       0x000000989EDFDFB8 (0)
		SQLPOINTER          0x000000989EDFDF58 (-1)
```

From research on the internet it seems this value should not matter for VARCHAR. The value passed by the code is `desc_record->sql_desc_scale` which was -1. Since the program would not run, I decided to hard code change to 0. I can not explain why, but at this point my program ran without exceptions, and I was then able to query tables without issue. 

I'm sorry that this leave a lot more questions than answers, and I don't have an easy github pull request. I also don't have a simple .Net app to reproduce the issue, but I may try to throw something together and add it here at some point. I will watch this issue and when I see changes I can test them here. Anyway, I'm hoping that what is here provides a good start to someone more familiar with DuckDB code and ODBC. 

I did figure out that the data used to populate these ODBC requests is coming from a call to `stmt->row_desc->GetIRD()->GetDescRecord(col_idx);` and that points to an instance of DescRecord defined in `M:\github\duckdb-v0.7.0\tools\odbc\include\descriptor.hpp`. I could not track down where that was getting populated. I'm guessing that the -1 values were defaults, but could not prove it. Also, my vbscript example does not make request for the same info as the System.Data.ODBC code, so that may be why this is not a problem for others...folks in .Net are probably using the .Net driver. 

Here is statement.cpp. Search for `cxb` to find the comments associated with changes, or you can diff or beyond compare with original file from v0.7.0.

[statement.cpp.txt](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/files/10755299/statement.cpp.txt)


### OS:

Windows

### DuckDB Version:

SQLite v0.7.0 f7827396d7

### DuckDB Client:

ODBC via .Net System.Data.ODBC

### Full Name:

charlie

### Affiliation:

none

### Have you tried this on the latest `master` branch?

- [X] I agree

### Have you tried the steps to reproduce? Do they include all relevant data and configuration? Does the issue you report still appear there?

- [X] I agree

review_comments:
In this case, the type_info behavior is slightly different from the SQLColAttribute behavior:
> This field is set to 0 for all non-numeric data types.

But is otherwise identical.
How would that work? Our columns only have names. Or are `name` and `label` ODBC specific?
I just want to look into what's possible in terms of specifying these, even if it's throwing a `SUCCESS_WITH_INFO`.
Is this a current bug or a `TODO`?
Is this the physical type? If it's the logical type, you can use `EnumUtil::ToString(col_type));`.
